title: Melting, Freezing, and the Phase Diagram of Water
outline:
The payoff chapter, and the strongest evidence in the book that these methods produce real physics rather than plausible pictures. Machine-learned potentials have produced full ab initio quality phase diagrams of water, homogeneous ice nucleation rates by seeding, the phase diagram and nucleation of gallium including its kinetic preference for the metastable beta phase, silicon crystallization from deep metadynamics, crystallization kinetics of the alloys used in phase-change memory, and evidence bearing on the disputed second critical point of supercooled water.

Built on the deep potential water phase diagram, ice nucleation by seeding, gallium and the Ostwald step rule made quantitative, Niu, Piaggi, Invernizzi and Parrinello on silica crystallization described accurately as to what the simulations did and did not resolve, phase-change memory alloys, and the second critical point controversy.

Leaves open: every one of these results depended on someone choosing the right coordinate to bias along.

verifiedClaims.claim: Joerg Behler and Michele Parrinello introduced the high-dimensional neural network potential, in which the total energy is decomposed into atomic contributions each predicted by an identical feed-forward network fed with symmetry-invariant functions of the local environment, demonstrating it on bulk silicon at a cost several orders of magnitude below DFT.
verifiedClaims.people: Jörg Behler, Michele Parrinello

verifiedClaims.claim: Albert P. Bartok, Mike C. Payne, Risi Kondor and Gabor Csanyi introduced Gaussian Approximation Potentials, applying Gaussian process regression to quantum-mechanical energies and forces so that the interatomic potential has no fixed functional form and can represent complex energy landscapes.
verifiedClaims.people: Albert P. Bartók, Mike C. Payne, Risi Kondor, Gábor Csányi
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Cavendish Laboratory, University of Cambridge

verifiedClaims.claim: Albert P. Bartok, James R. Kermode, Noam Bernstein and Gabor Csanyi built a general-purpose Gaussian Approximation Potential for silicon that reproduces DFT reference results simultaneously for crystalline, liquid and amorphous bulk phases as well as point, line and planar defects — a prerequisite for treating melting and crystallization within one model.
verifiedClaims.people: Albert P. Bartók, James Kermode, Noam Bernstein, Gábor Csányi

verifiedClaims.claim: Linfeng Zhang, Jiequn Han, Han Wang, Roberto Car and Weinan E introduced Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics (DeePMD), a deep neural network many-body potential that preserves the natural symmetries of the problem and scales linearly with system size while reproducing the ab initio training data essentially exactly.
verifiedClaims.people: Linfeng Zhang, Jiequn Han, Han Wang, Roberto Car, Weinan E

verifiedClaims.claim: Linfeng Zhang, Han Wang, Roberto Car and Weinan E computed the phase diagram of a Deep Potential water model trained on the SCAN density functional from low temperature and pressure up to roughly 2400 K and 50 GPa, correctly predicting the molecular and ionic fluid phases and all stable ice polymorphs, ordered and disordered, with the exception of ices III and XV which are stable in experiment but metastable in the model.
verifiedClaims.people: Linfeng Zhang, Han Wang, Roberto Car, Weinan E

verifiedClaims.claim: Bingqing Cheng, Edgar A. Engel, Joerg Behler, Christoph Dellago and Michele Ceriotti used a neural network potential together with free-energy methods to compute the ab initio thermodynamics of liquid water and ice, obtaining melting properties and the relative stability of the two phases at first-principles accuracy including nuclear quantum effects.
verifiedClaims.people: Bingqing Cheng, Edgar A. Engel, Jörg Behler, Christoph Dellago, Michele Ceriotti
verifiedClaims.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 116, 1110-1115

verifiedClaims.claim: Aleks Reinhardt and Bingqing Cheng computed the phase diagram of water at three hybrid density-functional levels of approximation, combining machine-learning potentials with advanced free-energy techniques and accounting for thermal fluctuations, nuclear quantum fluctuations and proton disorder; agreement with experiment is qualitative and best at pressures below roughly 8000 bar.
verifiedClaims.people: Aleks Reinhardt, Bingqing Cheng

verifiedClaims.claim: Bingqing Cheng, Guglielmo Mazzola, Chris J. Pickard and Michele Ceriotti used machine-learning interatomic potentials to overcome the system-size and timescale limits of ab initio molecular dynamics in dense hydrogen, finding evidence that the molecular-to-atomic transition in high-pressure liquid hydrogen is supercritical rather than a sharp first-order liquid-liquid transition over the range studied.
verifiedClaims.people: Bingqing Cheng, Guglielmo Mazzola, Chris J. Pickard, Michele Ceriotti

verifiedClaims.claim: Pablo G. Debenedetti, Francesco Sciortino and Gul H. Zerze presented computational evidence for a second, liquid-liquid critical point in deeply supercooled water in the TIP4P/2005 and TIP4P/Ice models, using histogram reweighting and large-system scattering calculations, with critical behaviour consistent with the three-dimensional Ising universality class.
verifiedClaims.people: Pablo G. Debenedetti, Francesco Sciortino, Gül H. Zerze

verifiedClaims.claim: Thomas E. Gartner III, Linfeng Zhang, Pablo M. Piaggi, Roberto Car, Athanassios Z. Panagiotopoulos and Pablo G. Debenedetti found signatures of a metastable liquid-liquid transition, with coexisting high-density and low-density liquid phases, in an ab initio deep neural network model of water trained on SCAN DFT data.
verifiedClaims.people: Thomas E. Gartner III, Linfeng Zhang, Pablo M. Piaggi, Roberto Car, Athanassios Z. Panagiotopoulos, Pablo G. Debenedetti
verifiedClaims.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 117, 26040-26046

verifiedClaims.claim: Pablo M. Piaggi, Jack Weis, Athanassios Z. Panagiotopoulos, Pablo G. Debenedetti and Roberto Car computed homogeneous ice nucleation rates at atmospheric pressure across a broad range of supercoolings using the seeding technique with a machine-learning model trained on DFT energies and forces, running systems of up to hundreds of thousands of atoms at ab initio accuracy.
verifiedClaims.people: Pablo M. Piaggi, Jack Weis, Athanassios Z. Panagiotopoulos, Pablo G. Debenedetti, Roberto Car
verifiedClaims.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 119, e2207294119

verifiedClaims.claim: Pablo M. Piaggi, Athanassios Z. Panagiotopoulos, Pablo G. Debenedetti and Roberto Car determined the phase equilibrium between liquid water and both hexagonal ice Ih and cubic ice Ic using a machine-learning potential trained on the SCAN functional, quantifying the small free-energy difference between the two ice polymorphs.
verifiedClaims.people: Pablo M. Piaggi, Athanassios Z. Panagiotopoulos, Pablo G. Debenedetti, Roberto Car
verifiedClaims.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation 17, 3065-3077

verifiedClaims.claim: Sigbjorn Loland Bore and Francesco Paesani combined the MB-pol data-driven many-body water potential with enhanced-sampling algorithms to compute water's phase diagram, obtaining close agreement with experiment for the stability fields of the ice polymorphs.
verifiedClaims.people: Sigbjørn Løland Bore, Francesco Paesani
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, University of California, San Diego

verifiedClaims.claim: Simon Batzner, Albert Musaelian, Lixin Sun, Mario Geiger, Jonathan P. Mailoa, Mordechai Kornbluth, Nicola Molinari, Tess E. Smidt and Boris Kozinsky introduced NequIP, an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network interatomic potential that matches or exceeds prior models while using up to three orders of magnitude less training data.
verifiedClaims.people: Simon Batzner, Albert Musaelian, Lixin Sun, Mario Geiger, Jonathan P. Mailoa, Mordechai Kornbluth, Nicola Molinari, Tess E. Smidt, Boris Kozinsky

verifiedClaims.claim: Albert Musaelian, Simon Batzner, Anders Johansson, Lixin Sun, Cameron J. Owen, Mordechai Kornbluth and Boris Kozinsky introduced Allegro, a strictly local equivariant deep neural network potential that represents many-body interactions through iterated tensor products of learned equivariant features without atom-centred message passing, enabling accurate simulations at very large scale.
verifiedClaims.people: Albert Musaelian, Simon Batzner, Anders Johansson, Lixin Sun, Cameron J. Owen, Mordechai Kornbluth, Boris Kozinsky

verifiedClaims.claim: Ilyes Batatia, David Peter Kovacs, Gregor N. C. Simm, Christoph Ortner and Gabor Csanyi introduced MACE, an equivariant message-passing architecture that carries higher body-order messages, overcoming the two-body limitation of conventional message-passing networks and yielding fast, accurate force fields.
verifiedClaims.people: Ilyes Batatia, Dávid Péter Kovács, Gregor N. C. Simm, Christoph Ortner, Gábor Csányi
verifiedClaims.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS) 2022; arXiv:2206.07697

verifiedClaims.claim: Ilyes Batatia and a large collaboration released MACE-MP-0, a single general-purpose MACE model trained on roughly 150,000 inorganic crystal structures from the Materials Project, which runs stable molecular dynamics across solids, liquids, gases, reactions and interfaces out of the box and can be fine-tuned on a handful of application-specific points.
verifiedClaims.people: Ilyes Batatia, Philipp Benner, Yuan Chiang, Alin M. Elena, Dávid P. Kovács, Janosh Riebesell, Xavier R. Advincula, Mark Asta, Matthew Avaylon, William J. Baldwin, Fabian Berger, Noam Bernstein, Arghya Bhowmik, Filippo Bigi, Samuel M. Blau, and others

verifiedClaims.claim: Alessandro Laio and Michele Parrinello introduced metadynamics, a coarse-grained non-Markovian dynamics in which a history-dependent bias potential progressively fills the free-energy minima of selected collective variables, allowing escape from metastable states and reconstruction of multidimensional free-energy surfaces — the enabling technique for simulating nucleation as a rare event.
verifiedClaims.people: Alessandro Laio, Michele Parrinello
verifiedClaims.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 99, 12562-12566

verifiedClaims.claim: Alessandro Barducci, Giovanni Bussi and Michele Parrinello introduced well-tempered metadynamics, in which the deposited bias is rescaled so that the history-dependent potential converges smoothly to a tunable fraction of the free energy rather than diffusing indefinitely.
verifiedClaims.people: Alessandro Barducci, Giovanni Bussi, Michele Parrinello

verifiedClaims.claim: Pablo M. Piaggi, Omar Valsson and Michele Parrinello showed that enhancing fluctuations of entropy and enthalpy — used as collective variables — drives crystallization in atomistic simulations, providing a general order parameter pair for first-order freezing transitions.
verifiedClaims.people: Pablo M. Piaggi, Omar Valsson, Michele Parrinello

verifiedClaims.claim: Pablo M. Piaggi and Michele Parrinello introduced multithermal-multibaric molecular simulations derived from a variational principle, in which a single simulation samples uniformly in energy and volume across a chosen region of the temperature-pressure plane, so that static properties and phase boundaries can be extracted for the whole region at once.
verifiedClaims.people: Pablo M. Piaggi, Michele Parrinello

verifiedClaims.claim: Michele Invernizzi, Pablo M. Piaggi and Michele Parrinello presented a unified approach to enhanced sampling — the on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling (OPES) framework — that reformulates metadynamics-style and generalized-ensemble methods as targeted probability-distribution reweighting.
verifiedClaims.people: Michele Invernizzi, Pablo M. Piaggi, Michele Parrinello

verifiedClaims.claim: Luigi Bonati and Michele Parrinello trained a deep neural network potential on SCAN-functional data, seeded by metadynamics sampling with a classical potential, and used a collective variable derived from the Debye structure factor to drive silicon crystallization, recovering the free-energy surface at DFT accuracy and probing the early stages of nucleation in a material whose liquid is metallic and whose solid is semiconducting.
verifiedClaims.people: Luigi Bonati, Michele Parrinello

verifiedClaims.claim: Haiyang Niu, Luigi Bonati, Pablo M. Piaggi and Michele Parrinello trained a neural network potential on DFT data drawn from multithermal-multibaric simulations to compute the ab initio phase diagram of gallium, reproducing the equilibria among liquid Ga, alpha-Ga, beta-Ga and Ga-II, and showed that formation of the metastable beta-Ga phase is kinetically favoured over the thermodynamically stable alpha-Ga.
verifiedClaims.people: Haiyang Niu, Luigi Bonati, Pablo M. Piaggi, Michele Parrinello

verifiedClaims.claim: Haiyang Niu, Pablo M. Piaggi, Michele Invernizzi and Michele Parrinello simulated the crystallization of liquid silica with enhanced-sampling molecular dynamics, resolving the nucleation pathway of a network-forming glass former.
verifiedClaims.people: Haiyang Niu, Pablo M. Piaggi, Michele Invernizzi, Michele Parrinello
verifiedClaims.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 115, 5348-5352

verifiedClaims.claim: Gabriele C. Sosso, Giacomo Miceli, Sebastiano Caravati, Joerg Behler and Marco Bernasconi built the first neural network interatomic potential for the phase-change memory material GeTe, reproducing DFT-quality descriptions of the liquid, crystalline and amorphous phases and opening large-scale simulation of technologically relevant crystallization.
verifiedClaims.people: Gabriele C. Sosso, Giacomo Miceli, Sebastiano Caravati, Jörg Behler, Marco Bernasconi

verifiedClaims.claim: Gabriele C. Sosso, Giacomo Miceli, Sebastiano Caravati, Federico Giberti, Joerg Behler and Marco Bernasconi used the neural network potential to run large-scale molecular dynamics of GeTe crystallization, quantifying the fast crystal growth that underlies phase-change memory operation.
verifiedClaims.people: Gabriele C. Sosso, Giacomo Miceli, Sebastiano Caravati, Federico Giberti, Jörg Behler, Marco Bernasconi
verifiedClaims.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters 4, 4241-4246

verifiedClaims.claim: Omar Abou El Kheir, Luigi Bonati, Michele Parrinello and Marco Bernasconi fitted a deep neural network potential to a large DFT database for Ge2Sb2Te5 and ran molecular dynamics on systems of over 10,000 atoms for more than 100 ns to resolve the crystallization kinetics of the compound across the range of temperatures relevant to memory devices.
verifiedClaims.people: Omar Abou El Kheir, Luigi Bonati, Michele Parrinello, Marco Bernasconi

verifiedClaims.claim: Volker L. Deringer, Noam Bernstein, Gabor Csanyi, Chiheb Ben Mahmoud, Michele Ceriotti, Mark Wilson, David A. Drabold and Stephen R. Elliott used a machine-learning potential to simulate transitions between disordered phases of silicon, predicting their electronic fingerprints and showing that pressure-induced crystallization of amorphous silicon proceeds through three distinct stages.
verifiedClaims.people: Volker L. Deringer, Noam Bernstein, Gábor Csányi, Chiheb Ben Mahmoud, Michele Ceriotti, Mark Wilson, David A. Drabold, Stephen R. Elliott

verifiedClaims.claim: Founding paper of classical nucleation theory: nucleus formation in supersaturated systems, introducing the capillarity/critical-nucleus argument that a droplet must exceed a critical size before it grows. Title translates as 'Nucleation in supersaturated structures'; commonly cited in English as 'Nucleus formation in supersaturated systems'. Z. Phys. Chem. volume is 119U (the 'U' denotes De Gruyter's retro-digitized series), issue 1, pages 277-301.
verifiedClaims.people: M. Volmer; A. Weber
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Volmer: Institute of Physical Chemistry, Technische Hochschule Berlin (Weber's affiliation not stated in the metadata I could access)

verifiedClaims.claim: First kinetic (rate) treatment of nucleation in supersaturated vapours, predating and feeding into Becker-Döring. 'Keimbildungsgeschwindigkeit in übersättigten Dämpfen', Z. Phys. Chem. 125U(1), 236-242. Useful if the chapter wants to show that the kinetic prefactor problem was posed before 1935.
verifiedClaims.people: L. Farkas
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Not verified from the source I could access

verifiedClaims.claim: The kinetic theory of nucleation: the cluster-population master equation and steady-state flux over the barrier that yields the Becker-Döring nucleation rate, J = A exp(-ΔG*/kT). CAUTION on the volume number: Annalen der Physik continuous vol. 416 = Band 24 of the 5. Folge, so 'Ann. Phys. 24, 719 (1935)' and 'Ann. Phys. 416, 719 (1935)' are the same paper. Issue 8, pages 719-752.
verifiedClaims.people: R. Becker; W. Döring
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Becker held the theoretical physics chair at Technische Hochschule Berlin and moved to Göttingen in the mid-1930s; Döring was his doctoral student. The paper's masthead affiliation was NOT verifiable (Wiley returned 403), so do not state an institution as fact.

verifiedClaims.claim: Transposes the vapour-condensation rate theory to condensed systems, using absolute-reaction-rate theory to supply the kinetic prefactor: I = A exp[-Kσ³/((ΔF_V)²kT)] with A = n(kT/h)exp(-ΔF_A/kT), where ΔF_A is the activation free energy for transporting an atom across the liquid-crystal interface. This is the paper that made nucleation theory usable for solidification. J. Chem. Phys. 17(1), 71-73. Note an errata was published at J. Chem. Phys. 17(4), 429 (1949) — see https://pubs.aip.org/aip/jcp/article/17/4/429/200784/Errata-Rate-of-Nucleation-in-Condensed-Systems .
verifiedClaims.people: David Turnbull; John C. Fisher
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Research Laboratory, General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York

verifiedClaims.claim: The droplet experiment itself: microscopic observation of the solidification of small metal droplets. Dispersing a melt into many tiny non-communicating droplets means most droplets contain no catalytic impurity, so homogeneous nucleation becomes observable. This is the experimental companion Turnbull cites (as ref. 2) for the supercooling data tabulated in his 1950 J. Appl. Phys. paper. J. Appl. Phys. 21(8), 804-810.
verifiedClaims.people: David Turnbull; R. E. Cech
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Research Laboratory, General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York

verifiedClaims.claim: THE supercooling paper — I read the reprint text and Table I directly. Maximum supercooling (ΔT_-)max in kelvin, with T0 in kelvin and the ratio (ΔT_-)max/T0: mercury 234.3 K / 58 K / 0.247; gallium 303 / 76 / 0.250; tin 505.7 / 105 / 0.208; bismuth 544 / 90 / 0.166; lead 600.7 / 80 / 0.133; antimony 903 / 135 / 0.150; aluminium 931.7 / 130 / 0.140; germanium 1231.7 / 227 / 0.184; silver 1233.7 / 227 / 0.184; gold 1336 / 230 / 0.172; copper 1356 / 236 / 0.174; manganese 1493 / 308 / 0.206; nickel 1725 / 319 / 0.185; cobalt 1763 / 330 / 0.187; iron 1803 / 295 / 0.164; palladium 1828 / 332 / 0.182; platinum 2043 / 370 / 0.181; water 273.2 / 39 / 0.143. Text states: 'For most metals (ΔT_-)max is of the order of 0.18 times the absolute melting temperature, T0', reproducible to ±5 percent, and later '≈0.185 with maximum deviations of ±0.02 ... the ratio ranges from 0.133 for lead to 0.250 for gallium.' Nucleation was measurable only over narrow bands: 59-63 degrees of supercooling for mercury, 100-115 for tin; fitted prefactors A = 10^30.4 (tin) and 10^30.9 (mercury) per cm³ per s, against 10^33 expected for homogeneous nucleation and 10^25 for surface-catalysed. 4-micron mercury droplets solidify at ~10^-5 s^-1 at ΔT = 60 K. Table II gives derived crystal-melt interfacial energies in erg/cm²: mercury 24.4, water 32.1, gallium 55.9, tin 54.5, bismuth 54.4, lead 33.3, antimony 101, aluminium 93, germanium 181, silver 126, gold 132, copper 177, manganese 206, nickel 255, cobalt 234, iron 204, palladium 209, platinum 240. J. Appl. Phys. 21(10), 1022-1028, received 13 April 1950.
verifiedClaims.people: David Turnbull
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Research Laboratory, General Electric Company, Schenectady, New York

verifiedClaims.claim: The definitive mercury-droplet kinetics study. Droplets 2-8 microns in diameter coated with mercury laurate solidify at rates proportional to droplet VOLUME (homogeneous nucleation); droplets coated with mercury acetate solidify at rates proportional to droplet AREA (heterogeneous nucleation) — the cleanest experimental separation of the two mechanisms. J. Chem. Phys. 20(3), 411-424. An erratum appeared at J. Chem. Phys. 20(11), 1824 (1952).
verifiedClaims.people: David Turnbull
verifiedClaims.affiliation: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York

verifiedClaims.claim: Equation-level, open-access source for the classical barrier that I verified by reading the text. Eq. (3): ΔG_n = n ΔG^nuc + n^(2/3) A σ; Eq. (5): n* = (-(2/3) Aσ/ΔG^nuc)³; Eq. (6): ΔG* = (4/27)(Aσ)³/(ΔG^nuc)², with A = (36π Ω1²)^(1/3) for a spherical cluster of monomer volume Ω1. Substituting A and ΔG^nuc = Ω1 Δg_v recovers exactly r* = 2γ/|Δg_v| and ΔG* = 16πγ³/(3 Δg_v²). Also has the clean Fig. 1/Fig. 2 distinction between the metastable (nucleation, G'' > 0) and unstable (spinodal, G'' < 0) regimes, which is precisely the framing a chapter deriving the barrier needs. ASM Handbook vol. 22A 'Fundamentals of Modeling for Metals Processing', D. U. Furrer and S. L. Semiatin (eds.), pp. 203-219; preprint on arXiv.
verifiedClaims.people: Emmanuel Clouet
verifiedClaims.affiliation: CEA Saclay, Service de Recherches de Métallurgie Physique, France
verifiedClaims.venue: ASM Handbook, Volume 22A: Fundamentals of Modeling for Metals Processing, pp. 203-219; arXiv:1001.4131

verifiedClaims.claim: The standard graduate monograph on nucleation — the reference to cite for the full CNT derivation (critical radius, barrier, Zeldovich factor, heterogeneous contact-angle factor) in book form. Pergamon Materials Series vol. 15, 756 pp., ISBN 978-0-08-042147-6 / 0-08-042147-4.
verifiedClaims.people: K. F. Kelton; A. Lindsay Greer
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Kelton: Washington University in St. Louis; Greer: University of Cambridge

verifiedClaims.claim: Standard review-article citation for CNT and its extensions, comparing theory against experiments that directly measure nucleation rates; covers condensation, cavitation and crystallization from the melt. J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 4(38), 7627-7650.
verifiedClaims.people: David W. Oxtoby
verifiedClaims.affiliation: James Franck Institute and Department of Chemistry, University of Chicago

verifiedClaims.claim: Modern review setting classical nucleation theory beside the nonclassical alternatives (density-functional and diffuse-interface approaches). Good single citation for 'the classical pathway is giving way to nonclassical pathways'. Cryst. Growth Des. 16(11), 6663-6681. I verified title, authors, journal, volume, pages and DOI, but could NOT open the full text to confirm it states the barrier in the exact r* = 2γ/Δg_v form — use Clouet or Kelton & Greer if you need the equation attributed to a specific page.
verifiedClaims.people: S. Karthika; T. K. Radhakrishnan; P. Kalaichelvi
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Department of Chemical Engineering, National Institute of Technology Tiruchirappalli, India

verifiedClaims.claim: Original statement of the step rule (Stufenregel): a supersaturated or supercooled system does not go directly to the most stable state but passes through the least stable state whose free energy is nearest to the starting state. Full title 'Studien über die Bildung und Umwandlung fester Körper. 1. Abhandlung: Übersättigung und Überkaltung' ('Studies on the formation and transformation of solid bodies. First paper: supersaturation and supercooling'). Z. Phys. Chem. 22U(1), 289-330.
verifiedClaims.people: Wilhelm Ostwald
verifiedClaims.affiliation: University of Leipzig

verifiedClaims.claim: Short, widely cited modern theoretical discussion of Ostwald's step rule, deriving it from irreversible thermodynamics — the standard 'why does the metastable phase appear first' citation. J. Phys. Chem. 88(24), 5768-5769.
verifiedClaims.people: R. A. van Santen
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Eindhoven University of Technology (the paper is deposited in the TU/e research portal)

verifiedClaims.claim: Direct atomic-scale experimental confirmation of Ostwald's rule of stages: in situ high-resolution electron microscopy at high temperature shows an amorphous olivine-type metal phosphate crystallizing to the stable phase through transient metastable crystalline intermediates. The best modern empirical citation for the step rule. Nature Physics 5(1), 68-73.
verifiedClaims.people: Sung-Yoon Chung; Young-Min Kim; Jin-Gyu Kim; Youn-Joong Kim
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Korea Basic Science Institute and Korean institutions (Chung later at KAIST / Sungkyunkwan; exact 2009 masthead affiliations not verified line-by-line)

verifiedClaims.claim: The gradient-energy free-energy functional F = ∫[f(c) + κ|∇c|²]dV — the origin of the diffuse-interface description of an interface and the direct ancestor of every phase-field model. 'Free Energy of a Nonuniform System. I. Interfacial Free Energy', J. Chem. Phys. 28(2), 258-267. Combined with the diffusion equation this gives the Cahn-Hilliard equation, ∂c/∂t = ∇·(M∇(∂f/∂c - 2κ∇²c)).
verifiedClaims.people: John W. Cahn; John E. Hilliard
verifiedClaims.affiliation: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York

verifiedClaims.claim: Part III of the same series: nucleation in a two-component incompressible fluid, worked with the diffuse-interface functional rather than the sharp-interface capillarity approximation. This is the paper to cite for the result that as the spinodal is approached the critical nucleus becomes large and diffuse and the barrier goes continuously to zero — i.e. the precise sense in which classical nucleation theory fails at the nucleation/spinodal crossover. J. Chem. Phys. 31(3), 688-699.
verifiedClaims.people: John W. Cahn; John E. Hilliard
verifiedClaims.affiliation: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York

verifiedClaims.claim: The spinodal decomposition paper: linear stability of a solid solution to infinitesimal composition fluctuations including gradient (surface tension) and elastic energy, giving the amplification-rate spectrum and the fastest-growing wavelength that sets the characteristic microstructural length scale. Acta Metallurgica 9(9), 795-801.
verifiedClaims.people: John W. Cahn
verifiedClaims.affiliation: General Electric Research Laboratory, Schenectady, New York

verifiedClaims.claim: 'Phase Separation by Spinodal Decomposition in Isotropic Systems' — the isotropic-system companion to the 1961 paper, the version usually cited for the treatment applicable to liquids and glasses rather than cubic crystals. J. Chem. Phys. 42(1), 93-99.
verifiedClaims.people: John W. Cahn
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Edgar C. Bain Laboratory for Fundamental Research, United States Steel Corporation (verify masthead if you print the affiliation; Cahn moved from GE to U.S. Steel in this period)

verifiedClaims.claim: Correct primary attribution for the Allen-Cahn equation: 'A microscopic theory for antiphase boundary motion and its application to antiphase domain coarsening', Acta Metallurgica 27(6), 1085-1095. The non-conserved order-parameter counterpart to Cahn-Hilliard; its key result is that the interfacial velocity is linearly proportional to the mean curvature of the boundary, with the constant of proportionality NOT containing the specific surface free energy. Author order is Allen then Cahn — 'Cahn-Allen' appears in some literature but the paper is Allen & Cahn.
verifiedClaims.people: Samuel M. Allen; John W. Cahn
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Allen: Department of Materials Science and Engineering, MIT; Cahn: National Bureau of Standards (now NIST). Masthead affiliations not verified line-by-line — verify before printing.

verifiedClaims.claim: THE specific quantified failure of CNT to cite. Argon condensation in a cryogenic supersonic nozzle at nucleation rates J = 10^(17±1) cm^-3 s^-1, over 34-53 K and 0.47-8 kPa: classical nucleation theory predicts rates 11-13 ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE LOWER than observed, while mean-field kinetic nucleation theory gets within 1 order of magnitude. The authors attribute the failure to CNT overestimating both the critical cluster size and the excess internal energy of the critical clusters. J. Chem. Phys. 132(6), 064304. Author order and full names confirmed via Crossref; the 11-13 figure comes from the published abstract as returned by the AIP/PubMed abstract text and should be re-read against the paper before quoting verbatim.
verifiedClaims.people: Somnath Sinha; Ashutosh Bhabhe; Hartawan Laksmono; Judith Wölk; Reinhard Strey; Barbara E. Wyslouzil
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Ohio State University (Sinha, Bhabhe, Laksmono, Wyslouzil) and Universität zu Köln, Institut für Physikalische Chemie (Wölk, Strey)

verifiedClaims.claim: The first parameter-free simulation prediction of an absolute crystal-nucleation rate (hard-sphere colloids), explicitly framed against CNT's need for unconstrained fitted parameters. This is the reference point for the hard-sphere rate discrepancy that follows. Nature 409, 1020-1023.
verifiedClaims.people: Stefan Auer; Daan Frenkel
verifiedClaims.affiliation: FOM Institute for Atomic and Molecular Physics (AMOLF), Amsterdam

verifiedClaims.claim: The hard-sphere colloid discrepancy, stated bluntly in the title: 'Simulation of nucleation in almost hard-sphere colloids: The discrepancy between experiment and simulation persists.' Independent simulation methods agree with each other and disagree with experiment. J. Chem. Phys. 134(13), 134901.
verifiedClaims.people: Laura Filion; Ran Ni; Daan Frenkel; Marjolein Dijkstra
verifiedClaims.affiliation: Soft Condensed Matter, Debye Institute for NanoMaterials Science, Utrecht University (Filion, Ni, Dijkstra); University of Cambridge (Frenkel)

verifiedClaims.claim: Quantifies the hard-sphere discrepancy in one sentence you can quote-check: 'at low super-saturations, experimentally observed nucleation rates and numerically computed ones differ by more than ten orders of magnitude.' Proposes resolving it by reading the experimental data as nucleation plus crystal growth rather than nucleation alone. Phys. Rev. Lett. 128(23), 238001; preprint arXiv:2205.06040 (2022), where I read the abstract.

corrections.claim: Invernizzi, Piaggi & Parrinello (2020), PRX 10, 041034 — 'presented a unified approach to enhanced sampling — the on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling (OPES) framework — that reformulates metadynamics-style and generalized-ensemble methods as targeted probability-distribution reweighting.'
corrections.correction: The citation (authors, order, year, venue, article number, DOI) is correct, but the claim misattributes the introduction of OPES. The PRX paper's own abstract states that it adapts 'the recently developed on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling method [Invernizzi and Parrinello, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 11.7 (2020)], which was originally introduced for metadynamics-like sampling.' Accurate replacement text: 'Michele Invernizzi, Pablo M. Piaggi and Michele Parrinello presented a unified perspective on enhanced sampling, focusing on the target probability distribution rather than the bias potential, and introduced a class of collective-variable-based bias potentials able to sample any expanded ensemble normally reached by replica exchange (OPES-expanded). Their practical implementation adapts the on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling (OPES) method, which had been introduced earlier that year by Michele Invernizzi and Michele Parrinello, "Rethinking Metadynamics: From Bias Potentials to Probability Distributions", Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters 11, 2731-2736 (2020).' URL for the PRX paper: https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.10.041034 ; URL for the paper that actually introduced OPES: https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.0c00497

corrections.claim: MACE-MP-0 is a general-purpose MACE model 'trained on roughly 150,000 inorganic crystal structures from the Materials Project'; cited only as arXiv:2401.00096.
corrections.correction: Two defects. (1) The training-set figure is garbled: MACE-MP-0 was trained on the Materials Project Trajectory (MPtrj) dataset, which contains 1,580,395 DFT structures drawn from roughly 146,000 inorganic materials covering 89 elements. The ~150,000 figure is the number of MATERIALS, not structures; the number of training structures is ~1.6 million (an order of magnitude larger). The paper's own abstract says only 'a public dataset of moderate size' and gives no such count. (2) The work is no longer preprint-only. Accurate replacement text: 'Ilyes Batatia and a large collaboration released MACE-MP-0, a single general-purpose MACE model trained on the Materials Project Trajectory (MPtrj) dataset — about 1.6 million DFT structures drawn from roughly 146,000 inorganic materials — which runs stable molecular dynamics across solids, liquids, gases, chemical reactions and interfaces out of the box and can be fine-tuned on a handful of application-specific data points to reach ab initio accuracy.' Correct citation: Ilyes Batatia, Philipp Benner, Yuan Chiang, Alin M. Elena, Dávid P. Kovács et al., 'A foundation model for atomistic materials chemistry', Journal of Chemical Physics 163(18), 184110 (2025), https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0297006 — preprint arXiv:2401.00096 (v1 29 December 2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.00096

corrections.claim: Invernizzi, Piaggi & Parrinello (2020) 'presented a unified approach to enhanced sampling — the on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling (OPES) framework'. PRX 10, 041034.
corrections.correction: The venue, authors, year and URL are correct, but the attribution overstates: the PRX paper did NOT introduce OPES. Its abstract explicitly states that it provides a practical implementation 'by properly adapting the iterative scheme of the recently developed on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling method [Invernizzi and Parrinello, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 11.7 (2020)], which was originally introduced for metadynamics-like sampling.' Accurate replacement text: 'Michele Invernizzi, Pablo M. Piaggi and Michele Parrinello presented a unified approach to enhanced sampling, recasting collective-variable bias methods (umbrella sampling, metadynamics) and tempering/expanded-ensemble methods such as replica exchange within one perspective focused on the target probability distribution, and implemented it by adapting the iterative scheme of the on-the-fly probability enhanced sampling (OPES) method.' Cite as: Michele Invernizzi, Pablo M. Piaggi, Michele Parrinello, 'Unified Approach to Enhanced Sampling', Physical Review X 10, 041034 (2020), https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.10.041034. OPES itself must be credited to: Michele Invernizzi and Michele Parrinello, 'Rethinking Metadynamics: From Bias Potentials to Probability Distributions', Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters 11, 2731-2736 (2020), https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.0c00497

corrections.claim: Kelton & Greer, Pergamon Materials Series vol. 15, 756 pp., ISBN 978-0-08-042147-6 / 0-08-042147-4, 2010 — the standard graduate monograph on nucleation

F.) Kelton and Alan Lindsay Greer), but the dossier entry OMITS THE TITLE entirely, giving only a description. A reference list built from this entry would be unusable. The full title is 'Nucleation in Condensed Matter: Applications in Materials and Biology'. corrections.claim: van Santen 1984, 'The Ostwald step rule', J. Phys. Chem. 88(24), 5768-5769; author affiliated with Eindhoven University of Technology
corrections.correction: The bibliography is right; THE AFFILIATION IS WRONG. Crossref confirms R. A. Van Santen, 'The Ostwald step rule', The Journal of Physical Chemistry volume 88, issue 24, pages 5768-5769, November 1984, DOI 10.1021/j150668a002. But the affiliation printed on the paper is Koninklijke Shell-Laboratorium, Shell Research B.V., Amsterdam, The Netherlands — NOT Eindhoven University of Technology. The dossier inferred Eindhoven from the paper sitting in the TU/e research portal, which hosts it only because van Santen moved to TU/e later (1986). This is exactly the failure mode the dossier warned about elsewhere. Do not print 'Eindhoven' for this paper. The substantive claim is CONFIRMED: the paper relates Ostwald's step rule to irreversible thermodynamics and argues the step rule minimizes entropy production.

corrections.claim: Cahn, 'Phase Separation by Spinodal Decomposition in Isotropic Systems', J. Chem. Phys. 42(1), 93-99 (1965); affiliation Edgar C. Bain Laboratory for Fundamental Research, United States Steel Corporation, with the note that 'Cahn moved from GE to U.S. Steel in this period'
corrections.correction: The bibliography is right; THE AFFILIATION AND THE CAREER CLAIM ARE WRONG. Crossref confirms 'Phase Separation by Spinodal Decomposition in Isotropic Systems', John W. Cahn, JCP volume 42, issue 1, pages 93-99, January 1965, DOI 10.1063/1.1695731. But John W. Cahn never worked at U.S. Steel's Edgar C. Bain Laboratory. His documented chronology is General Electric, Schenectady 1954-1964; MIT Department of Metallurgy 1964-1978; National Bureau of Standards from 1977; University of Washington affiliate from 1984 (confirmed by his Wikipedia entry, the NAE Memorial Tributes vol. 22 entry, and obituary coverage — none of which mention U.S. Steel). He moved from GE to MIT in 1964, not to U.S. Steel. I could not open the printed masthead of JCP 42, 93 (AIP returns 403 and ADS blocks fetch), so the correct affiliation is GE or MIT depending on the submission date — DO NOT PRINT ANY AFFILIATION for this paper without reading the masthead, and delete the U.S. Steel parenthetical.

corrections.claim: Royall, Charbonneau, Dijkstra, Russo, Smallenburg, Speck & Valeriani, Rev. Mod. Phys. 96, 045003 (2024); multi-institutional (ESPCI Paris, Duke, Utrecht, Bristol, CNRS/Paris-Saclay, Stuttgart, Complutense Madrid)
corrections.correction: Bibliography confirmed: 'Colloidal hard spheres: Triumphs, challenges, and mysteries', author order exactly as the dossier lists, Reviews of Modern Physics volume 96, issue 4, article number 045003, 12 November 2024, DOI 10.1103/RevModPhys.96.045003. THE AFFILIATION LIST IS INCOMPLETE: Crossref gives Royall at ESPCI Paris and University of Bristol, Charbonneau at Duke, Dijkstra at Utrecht, Russo at Sapienza University of Rome, Smallenburg at Université Paris-Saclay, Speck at Universität Stuttgart, Valeriani at Universidad Complutense de Madrid. The dossier's list omits Sapienza University of Rome (John Russo) — Bristol is Royall's second affiliation, not Russo's. Also note the dossier's own caveat is sound: it did not read the full text, so do not attribute the ten-orders-of-magnitude number or the enumeration of failed explanations (polydispersity, residual charge, hydrodynamics, sedimentation, volume-fraction calibration) to this review as verified content — cite Wöhler & Schilling for the number.

corrections.claim: ten Wolde & Frenkel, Science 277(5334), 1975-1978 (1997): a metastable fluid-fluid critical point drastically changes the pathway to a crystal nucleus, lowering the barrier and raising the rate by many orders of magnitude; 'the canonical citation for the reaction coordinate is not the nucleus radius'
corrections.correction: The bibliography is exactly right — Crossref confirms Pieter Rein ten Wolde; Daan Frenkel, Science volume 277, issue 5334, pages 1975-1978, 26 September 1997, DOI 10.1126/science.277.5334.1975 — and the physics is right: the abstract states that in simulations of homogeneous crystal nucleation, the presence of a metastable fluid-fluid critical point drastically changes the pathway for formation of a crystal nucleus, and that close to that critical point the free-energy barrier is strongly reduced so the nucleation rate increases by many orders of magnitude. THE PROBLEM IS THE MISSING TITLE AND THE RESULTING SCOPE DRIFT: the paper is 'Enhancement of Protein Crystal Nucleation by Critical Density Fluctuations', and the result is obtained for a model of globular proteins with short-range attractive interactions, not for nucleation in general. The dossier presents it as a generic 'two-step / nonclassical nucleation result' with no title given; a chapter citing it should print the title and say 'in a model of globular proteins with short-range attractions'. The 'reaction coordinate is not the nucleus radius' line is a defensible gloss but is the chapter's phrasing, not the paper's — do not put it in quotation marks.
